record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How many words of a given length contain a strongly k-abelian nth power?

evidence.quote: How many words of a given length contain a strongly k-abelian nth power?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $k, n \geq 2$ integers. Two finite words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_k v$, if for every word $x \in \Sigma^*$ with $|x| \leq k$, the number of occurrences of $x$ as a factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $x$ as a factor of $v$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called a strongly $k$-abelian $n$th power if there exist words $u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_n \in \Sigma^*$ such that $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n$ and $u_i \sim_k u_j$ for all $1 \leq i, j \leq n$.

For fixed $\Sigma$, $k$, and $n$, determine, as a function of $\ell$, the number of words $w \in \Sigma^\ell$ of length $\ell$ that contain a factor which is a strongly $k$-abelian $n$th power. Equivalently, give a closed-form or asymptotic enumeration of such words.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches concerning strongly k-abelian repetitions show that they are known to be unavoidable on every alphabet for all k, n, but no enumeration formula or asymptotic count for the number of length-ℓ words containing a strongly k-abelian nth power was located in the available literature. The status of this enumeration problem appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly k-abelian nth powers are not avoidable on any alphabet for any numbers k.
status_evidence.claim: Unavoidability is established, but no enumeration of words containing such powers is provided.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Combinatorics on Words: a Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian combinatorics on words including k-abelian variants.
status_evidence.claim: A recent survey covers k-abelian topics but does not report a counting formula for words containing strongly k-abelian nth powers.
